said.meaning: draw the letters of the judgment words first (before the numerals)

letters.P: stem 30 and a bowl from 34 up: square on the left, rounded as the O on the right; lower bar 24, upper 26 (width 96)
letters.E: stem and three arms 24 thick (middle one 8 shorter), right ends cut at 52 degrees like the right end of the T (width 84)
letters.R: the bowl of the P (width 100) and a leg 30 across at 52 degrees under it, 6 below the bowl (stencil, as the leg of the K), reaching the baseline at the right
letters.F: the E without its lower arm (width 82)
letters.C: the O 96 wide, open on the right between y 26 and 74 (flat ends)
letters.G: the O 104 wide, open on the upper right between 56 and 74, the lower right of the counter filled up to 56 as a spur
letters.A: vertical legs 30, top corners cut 52 tall at 52 degrees (deeper than the usual 26) so that it reads as A and not as 4, top 26, crossbar 24 at 24 to 48, open at the bottom (width 112)
letters.D: stem on the left, rounded as the O on the right (width 100)
letters.M: two stems 30 and a V standing 6 apart from them, its arms 30 across on the axis of the diagonal of the N (width 136)
letters.S: two rings stacked (y 38 to 100 and 0 to 62, bars 24), the upper open on the right, the lower open on the left (width 96)

notes: horizontals: 26 in O, C, G, D, T and the upper bar of a bowl; 24 in E, F, S, the lower bar of a bowl and the crossbar of the A
counters of P, R, E, S are 14 to 16 tall: fine at the large sizes of judgment words, may fill in small
setting: the four words set with nothing but the gap of 6 (no script, no sweeps)
